value.0: The record stands at one pass: yours. The last one I issued held the bottom of a crypt for years before you revoked it for me. I never praise twice, and I have already spent yours. Go and be the verdict I do not have to correct.

You hesitated at the door. That hesitation is a grade, and you failed it. The Eclipse of Resolve is not offered to candidates whose command of the Force is still a work in progress. Complete your mastery of it. Then present yourself for examination. If you still dare to.

You carried a doubt through that door. Do not deny it; denial is a second doubt, and I grade cumulatively. Good. Doubt is the raw material of this examination. Below us, in the Korriban Sith Crypt Depths, a cell of my former candidates rehearses the Eclipse of Resolve they failed to earn. Six adepts, drilling a doctrine they were never passed on. Cull all six and confiscate the Eclipse of Resolve Crypt Trial Tablet they teach from. That is your first paper. Submit it complete or not at all.

Accepted and logged. The stair key is yours; it opens the sealed descent into the Korriban Sith Crypt Depths. Six adepts, one tablet, no partial credit. And candidate, mind the crypt itself. Korriban enjoys grading people, and it marks harder than I do.

In my words, since yours would mangle it: resolve that admits no fear-light whatsoever. Not courage. Courage coexists with fear. An eclipse. The will passes in front of everything else and the mind goes usefully dark. Done correctly, hesitation becomes physically impossible. Done incorrectly, you get what festers below us: candidates who eclipsed their judgment instead. The examination exists to tell the difference.

Six adepts I examined and failed, who chose to grade themselves instead. They fled down the sealed stair into the crypt depths and continued the curriculum without supervision. The key I issue you opens that stair. Follow the descent past the first tombs to the rite-chambers. They will be reciting. They were always better at reciting than at understanding.

Prepare for candidates with nothing left to lose academically. A failed adept fights worse than a passed one, but harder; desperation is poor technique with excellent attendance. Six of them, in crypts that amplify fear, which is the one resource you must not bring. If you feel the dark pressing in, treat it as part of the test. It is. Everything is.
Your first paper remains unsubmitted. Six adepts still recite below, and their tablet still teaches error. I have seen candidates stall at this stage. I failed all of them.
Six struck from the rolls, and the tablet out of circulation. Hand it to me. I will assess how much damage they did to the text.

Assessment: the text is corrupted, the corruption is contained, and the candidate returned intact. Provisional pass. Do not glow. Provisional is the highest grade this stage offers. Your credits, per the standard schedule. The next examination is available whenever your nerve is. Bring less doubt than you brought today. I counted.

You returned for the second paper. Noted without comment. Deeper in the crypt depths, five specialists maintain the failed cell's focus, the Eclipse of Resolve Ritual Focus Shard. They pour their fear into it nightly and call the emptiness that remains resolve. It is not resolve. It is amputation. Destroy the five, confiscate the shard, and return it to me for doctrinal review.

Logged. Five specialists, one shard, standard descent through your previous work. One instruction, and I will not repeat it: pour nothing of yours into that stone, whatever it offers to hold for you. It has excellent references and no intention of giving anything back.

It proves my thesis, which is why I want it preserved. True eclipse is the will outshining fear. The fear remains present, simply irrelevant. The specialists instead decant their fear into a stone and congratulate themselves on feeling nothing. Feeling nothing is not passing. That shard is five students' worth of discarded fear in one object. As doctrinal evidence, it is a signed confession.

Below the chambers you cleared, where the galleries narrow. They cluster around the shard because they must; separated from it, their discarded fear starts finding its way home. You will see the glow before you see them. Walk into it deliberately. Candidates who creep toward that light arrive already failing.

Fearlessly, in the defective sense. They cannot retreat. Retreat requires the fear they threw away. So they will press you in waves, without self-preservation, and undisciplined aggression from five directions defeats most candidates through arithmetic alone. Keep your footing, spend their recklessness against them, and remember which one of you can still choose to be careful. That choice is the entire examination.
The second paper sits incomplete. Five specialists, one shard, and a growing suspicion on my part that you are drafting excuses. Disprove it.
The shard, and a candidate still in possession of their own fear. Correct on both counts. Surrender the stone.

Graded and archived. The shard confirms everything I have taught over their objections: emptiness is not eclipse. You begin to be evidence for the doctrine instead of against it, which is the first useful thing most candidates ever accomplish. Credits per schedule. The third examination has a proctor, and he does not share my restraint.

The third paper is a practical, so I will state the format plainly. The breach into the deep tombs is held by the failed cell's warden. My most promising failure. A candidate whose eclipse was total and totally misaimed, and he wears the Eclipse of Resolve Splintered Tomb Sigil as if it were a diploma. Retrieve it. And record this examination condition, because I wrote it: the practical is not sat alone. A resolve tested against one opponent is barely tested. Bring two examinees whose nerve has already been graded. He has ended every solitary candidate I sent, and I sent several.

Condition accepted. The examination is live. Direct your two: spread his attention, never his footing. He cannot be moved, but he can be overtaxed. When he falls, collect every splinter of the sigil. An incomplete exhibit is an incomplete grade, and you know my policy on partial credit.

Precision. His eclipse was flawless in form. Will out front, fear irrelevant, hesitation extinct. I nearly passed him. Then I saw what his will had fixed upon: the doorway itself. Holding it. Forever. Against everything, for nothing. A perfect instrument aimed at a meaningless target. I failed him, and he appealed the verdict by moving into the breach. He has been appealing it ever since.

Because I do not design tests that measure luck. One fighter against the warden measures whether he blinks, and he does not blink. I removed that from him myself. Three coordinated wills against his one measures something real: whether resolve can be shared without dimming. Most candidates cannot manage it. Their eclipse admits no colleagues. If yours can, you will have passed a section most never even see.

The tomb seal he swore his eclipse to. It splintered when the deep doors were forced, and he keeps the pieces as proof that his vigil continues. Which is to say, as proof that he cannot admit an ended thing has ended. Doctrinally, it is the most instructive object in the crypt: resolve outliving its reason. Bring it to me and I will show the next generation what that costs.
The warden still holds the breach, and your third paper with it. Three examinees, no fewer. A solo attempt will be graded posthumously.
You return, your companions return, and the breach stands empty. The sigil. All of it.

Denied and closed, after years of my failures dying in its service. I will say this once, so listen carefully: adequate work. That is the only time you will hear it. The sigil joins the record, your credits join your account, and the fourth examination joins your schedule. The inner circle wrote the corrupted curriculum. You will now retract it.

The fourth paper: retraction. Four remain of the cell's inner circle, the authors of the corrupted doctrine. Senior candidates who decided that failing my examination qualified them to administer their own. They hold the Eclipse of Resolve Keeper's Rite Token and use it to ordain new students into their error. Expunge all four and confiscate the token. When a doctrine cannot be corrected, it is withdrawn from circulation, and they are long past correcting.

Logged and live. They know their warden fell, and they know their curriculum is being audited chamber by chamber. Expect them prepared, entrenched, and certain. Certainty without examination is just volume. Lower theirs. Bring me the token when four signatures have been struck from my record.

A forgery with excellent penmanship. They kept my structure, the trials, the proofs, the ordinations, and inverted the content. Where I teach the will to outshine fear, they teach the student to burn out the part that fears. Their graduates are the adepts and specialists you removed. Fearless the way the dead are fearless. Four authors, one plagiarized doctrine, an entire cell of ruined students. That is their bibliography.

It is my token. I struck it years ago to mark candidates approved to teach, and the circle's founders stole it when they fled below. Every ordination since has been a forgery bearing my seal. You see now why this examination is not optional, for either of us. Recover it, and the last thing legitimizing their curriculum returns to the only hand holding actual authority.

One recommendation, not a condition. You have earned the distinction. They defend the token as a single body, four wills braided into one doctrine, and braided wills unravel from the ends. Whichever of them breaks formation first is the thread to cut. If you bring your two from the breach, so much the better. I no longer grade whether you need others. I grade the others fortunate.
Four authors still hold my token and still ordain students into ruin. The retraction stands incomplete. I dislike open files.
Struck, all four. And my token, back within reach after years of being forged against me. Hand it over.

Retraction complete. The curriculum below is authorless, its ordinations void, its enrollment ended by your hand. The record will show the doctrine was defended. It will not show gratitude; that is not a field on the form. Credits per schedule. One examination remains, and I will be honest with you for the first time: I do not know whether it can be passed.

The final examination. At the bottom of the crypt depths waits the master. The first candidate I ever examined for the Eclipse of Resolve, and the only one whose eclipse I could not fault. I passed him. Everything rotting below is what my verdict built. He wields the doctrine entire, the true eclipse, fear rendered permanently irrelevant, and for years it has aimed itself at nothing but its own continuation. There is no exhibit to recover. His defeat is the verdict. Final condition, and you already know it: this examination is sat in threes. A resolve untested against many is untested, and he is many all by himself.

The examination is convened. Descend with your two, and disregard everything the crypt promises or threatens on the way down. It is not on the committee. When you face him, do not wait for doubt to leave you. It will not, and it should not. Doubt attending the eclipse, and overruled. That is the doctrine done correctly. Show him.

Nothing went wrong with the eclipse. That is the horror of it, and the final lesson. The doctrine worked. His will outshone fear so completely that nothing remained to tell him when to stop willing. Resolve requires an object, something to be resolved toward, and he burned through every object he had. Now the eclipse sustains itself. What eclipsed his resolve was his resolve. Write that down somewhere you will reread it.

Then the record shows one pass, and that pass holds the bottom of a crypt until Korriban wears away. I do not examine for sentiment, but understand what you carry down that stair: every verdict I have ever issued rests on whether this doctrine can produce something other than him. You are the retrial of my life's work. I suggest you find that motivating rather than heavy. That is also part of the test.

You do not outlast it, and you cannot frighten it. You present it with a problem resolve cannot solve alone: three wills that keep each other's fear alive. Yes, alive. Your fear tells you when he is about to end you. He has no such adviser. Rotate his attention, shield whoever he fixes upon, and be, together, more adaptable than one perfect will. If the doctrine is sound, that is enough. If it is not, then I have graded everything wrong. Including you.
The final examination remains open. The master waits at the bottom, and the condition stands: three examinees. There is nothing to retrieve. There is only the verdict.
You stand in front of me, which means the bottom of the crypt no longer holds a pass of mine. Report the verdict.

Then the record amends: one pass revoked, one pass entered. Yours. I told you I never praise twice, so hold still and hear it the once. You carried doubt into the dark, and your resolve eclipsed it without killing it. That is the doctrine, whole, and it is now yours, verified. Examination concluded. Leave before I am tempted to say something kind again.
Restate the assignment.
Then grade this: six adepts, one tablet, done.
What is the Eclipse of Resolve, in your own words?
Who are these failed candidates?
What should I prepare for down there?
I'll submit when I'm ready. Not before.
Here's their tablet. The recitals have stopped.
Back to the paper.
Five specialists. Their shard goes on your desk.
What does the shard prove?
Where will I find them?
How do they fight?
I'll sit this paper after I've reviewed my notes.
One shard, untouched by me. The five are graded.
Back to the practical.
Then we sit it together. Three of us, one warden.
What made him your most promising failure?
Why do you insist on three examinees?
What is the sigil evidence of?
I'll assemble my examinees first.
Every splinter. His appeal is denied.
Back to the retraction.
Four authors, one retraction. Consider it in progress.
What did the inner circle actually teach?
And the token ordains them?
Four at once. Any examination conditions?
The retraction can wait a day.
Your token, out of forgery. The circle is retracted.
Back to the examination.
Then convene it. Three of us will sit the trial.
What went wrong, if his eclipse was flawless?
What happens to your record if we fail?
How do we fight a flawless eclipse?
My examinees need preparation. The trial waits.
The master failed. We stood, all three of us.
